resale_co.name: Certificate of Occupancy for Sale (Sales C.O.), resale Housing Code inspection
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Palmyra Department of Housing (Housing Official)
resale_co.lead_time: Pay the fee before the inspection is scheduled. By ordinance the Borough schedules the inspection no later than 7 business days after the application and fee; an inspection within 5 business days costs $50 extra and within 3 business days $100 extra. Allow 48 hours after the inspection for the report.
resale_co.valid_for: Not stated. If the home fails, a Temporary Sales C.O. may allow occupancy for up to 60 days (extendable by up to 30 days) when the violations do not threaten health or safety.
requirements: Review of required permits along with the inspection
Interior: structural members, interior surfaces, lead-based paint, stairs, railings (including attic and basement), handrails and guards
Anti-tip bracket on the oven
Exterior: paint, street numbers (Arabic numerals at least 3 inches high), foundation, walls, roof, gutters and downspouts, chimneys, porches, decks and stairs (sidewalks not inspected)
Windows open and stay open; no broken glass; insect screens; deadbolt locks on doors; basement hatch and basement window guards
Yard: sanitation, grading and drainage, weeds under 6 inches, no rodent harborage, no unregistered or junk vehicles, firewood stored off the ground, fences in good condition
Plumbing fixtures, water heater, exhaust fan and drainage in working order
Heat, HVAC, washer and dryer, flue and combustion air; electrical hazards, GFCI outlets where required, covers and switch plates, no open junction boxes
Borough green trash carts; no rubbish, no infestation
Means of egress, locked doors, emergency escape
Smoke detectors on each level including basement and walk-up attic, outside each sleeping area within 10 feet, not in the kitchen; 10-year sealed lithium battery type
CO detectors within 10 feet of sleeping areas
One 2A:10B:C fire extinguisher in the kitchen (not mounted), bought within a year with receipt or tagged (January 2022 checklist still lists it)
Smoke/CO certificate under N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.3 is also required before any sale (separate Fire Marshal inspection)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Resale Inspection Application for Certificate of Occupancy (one per unit) and turn it in at Borough Hall, 20 W. Broad Street, with the $125.00 fee payable to the Borough of Palmyra (check or cash). Then call (856) 829-1096 to schedule. Palmyra Harbour condominiums use a separate application.

evidence.quote: Attention Homeowners: thinking of selling your home? Effective April 1, 2014, Certificate of Occupancy inspections (on existing home re-sales) are now required.
Please register your rental unit with Housing Official Tracy Kilmer and submit your Certificate of Occupancy Application to Housing Official Tracy Kilmer.
To schedule a rental property or Certificate of Occupancy inspection (on existing home re-sales) please call (856) 829-1096.
This memo shall serve as a request for a Housing Code Inspection regarding the above referenced property for sale.
BOROUGH OF PALMYRA Department of Housing 20 W. Broad Street Palmyra, NJ 08065 Phone: 856-829-1096 Email: tkilmer@boroughofpalmyra.com
NOTE: PLEASE ALLOW 48 HOURS FOR INSPECTION REPORT RESULTS TO BE AVAILABLE.
IN ADDITION TO THE INSPECTION A REVIEW OF REQUIRED PERMITS WILL BE COMPLETED.
Except as set forth below, upon the sale of a residence, no person shall occupy the residence until the Borough issues a Sales C.O. for the residence.
If one or more of the sellers of the residence is 65 years of age or older on the date of sale; or
The required fee shall cover an initial inspection in the event of a failure of the first inspection.
the Borough shall schedule an inspection of the residence, no later than seven business days from the submission of the required form and fees.

Notwithstanding anything contained herein to the contrary, no residence shall be sold unless it has been inspected and approved pursuant to N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.3 (smoke detectors and carbon monoxide alarms).

resale_co.notes: Palmyra requires a Sales Certificate of Occupancy (Housing Code inspection) on home resales: Borough Code Chapter 93 (Ord. No. 2015-10, effective July 30, 2015, read in full through the ecode360 print view) and the Borough housing page ('Effective April 1, 2014'). The ordinance fee is 'not to exceed $125'; the application form and web page charge $125 per unit, which covers the first inspection and one reinspection; later inspections are $25 each. Exceptions in the ordinance: if a seller is 65 or older, totally disabled, or has been in an assisted-care or nursing facility for at least 30 days before the sale, the home may be occupied for up to 180 days after the sale before the Sales C.O. is needed, but the state smoke/CO certificate is still required before occupancy. The application PDF was created June 2022 and the checklist is REV DATE 01/20/2022. The same checklist covers home resales and rental tenant turnover; rental registration ($125) is a rental program, not a resale requirement. Validity of the Sales C.O. is not published.

requirements: Battery or hard-wired smoke detector on each level (minimum); hard-wired systems must work
Smoke detectors over 10 years old will not pass; resale/rental battery alarms must be 10-year sealed units
No detector in the kitchen area
Smoke detector and carbon monoxide detector outside each sleeping area
Third floor or attic with walk-up steps needs a smoke and CO detector, used or not
One ABC 2A:10B:C portable fire extinguisher in the kitchen, tagged within the year or with a receipt showing purchase within a year; need not be mounted (Borough page still lists it)

authorities.name: Palmyra Bureau of Fire Prevention (Borough Fire Marshal)
authorities.lead_time: Fee depends on how many days before settlement/change of occupancy the inspection is requested: more than 10 days for the lowest fee. Inspections Monday to Thursday, 9:00am to 12 noon. A new application is needed if the change of occupancy does not happen within six months (Borough Code).

fees.label: Smoke/CO certificate, requested more than 10 days before settlement
fees.quote: For inspections requested more than 10 days prior to settlement/change of occupancy: $45.00

fees.label: Requested 4 to 10 days before settlement
fees.quote: For inspections requested 4 and 10 days prior to settlement/change of occupancy: $90.00

fees.label: Requested less than 4 days before settlement
fees.quote: For inspections less than 4 days prior to settlement/change of occupancy: $161.00

authorities.how_to_apply: There is no written application. Call the Fire Marshal's Office at (856) 829-1096 to schedule the smoke/CO inspection (Monday to Thursday, 9:00am to 12 noon). No fee is charged for a second reinspection. This is separate from the $125 Sales C.O. housing inspection.
authorities.contact_title: Fire Marshal (Fire Official; also Housing Official and Fire Sub Code Official)

evidence.quote: If you are selling or changing occupancy of your one- or two-family dwelling then a Certificate of Smoke Detector/Carbon Monoxide Alarm and Fire Extinguisher is required.
There is no written application prior to the inspection. Simply call the Fire Marshal’s Office and we will schedule a date and time for inspection.
Inspections are done Monday thru Thursday, 9:00am to 12 noon.
No fee will be assessed for a second reinspection.

no owner shall sell, lease or otherwise permit occupancy for residential purpose of that building without first obtaining from the Borough Fire Official a certificate evidencing compliance with the requirements of the article.
For requests received more than 10 business days prior to the sale, rental or change of occupant: $45.
For requests received fewer than four business days prior to the sale, rental or change of occupant: $161.
The Bureau operates under the Fire Marshal Tracy Kilmer.
SMOKE DETECTORS WILL NOT PASS INSPECTION IF OVER 10 YEARS OF AGE!
M Palmyra Borough
Fire Official Tracy L Kilmer Phone (856) 829-1096 Addr: 20 W Broad St
Email tkilmer@boroughofpalmyra.com

fire_cert.notes: Palmyra Borough is its own fire code enforcing agency (M in the DCA LEA registry, July 2026). The smoke/CO certificate is a separate Fire Marshal inspection with its own fee ($45 / $90 / $161, set by Borough Code §121-14 as amended May 21, 2018, and posted on the Borough housing page). The Borough page counts 'days prior to settlement'; the ordinance says business days. Tracy Kilmer is both Fire Marshal and Housing Official. The Fire Marshal email is hidden on the Borough page and is taken from the state directory (January 2023 survey). The extinguisher is still listed on the Borough housing and Fire Marshal pages. The state removed the portable fire extinguisher from the sale certificate requirement in February 2025 (P.L.2025, c.19). Ask the office whether it is still enforced.

other_items.label: Flood risk disclosure
other_items.detail: The Borough's 'Resale/Rental Additional Requirements' form: since March 20, 2024 sellers must give the buyer the flood risk information (Property Condition Disclosure Statement: Flood Risk Notice, N.J.S.A. 46:8-50) before the buyer is bound by the contract.

other_items.label: Open permits
other_items.detail: A review of required permits is done with the CO inspection.

other_items.label: Seller age or disability exception
other_items.detail: If a seller is 65 or older, totally disabled, or has been in a care facility at least 30 days before the sale, the buyer may occupy for up to 180 days before the Sales C.O. is issued; the smoke/CO certificate is still needed first.
